corrections.why: The Coast Guard list and the Town of Prescott both give the tower as 6.8 m. The record's 6.0 m comes from Wikidata.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list calls the light Prescott Heritage Harbour and the Town calls it the Heritage Harbour Lighthouse. The record and Wikidata call it Prescott Breakwater Lighthouse. The Lighthouse Digest places a light on the breakwater separately from the Rotary Light, which it calls the Prescott Harbor Inner Light. The outer light is the one at the harbour mouth; the record's name is kept.

notes_for_editor: 1) No first-lit date, build date, designer or cost was found. The Marine corpus for 1900-1924 names the Prescott depot many times but no breakwater light by name. Web sources gave nothing on the light's construction. The story is short for that reason. A Prescott local history or a 1950s-1980s Coast Guard list may hold the date. 2) LighthouseFriends' build date ('late 1908s') is garbled and was not used. 3) The record's 6.0 m height (Wikidata) disagrees with the Coast Guard and the Town (6.8 m). The record's wood material is repeated by two search-result listings we did not read as pages, so it is left out of the story. 4) The Dominion Lighthouse Depot was a depot, not a light; it has no record here. The story mentions it only as the Prescott context the sources give. 5) Windmill Point Lighthouse, named in a Beautiful Ontario article (search snippet, not read) as the site of an 1838 battle, is a different light and is not covered here. 6) The Lighthouse Digest is a magazine article; facts only. 7) The Rotary Lighthouse (1989) is a replica with a restored lantern; it is a separate structure and not an aid to navigation in the Coast Guard list. 8) Whether the breakwater itself is open to walk on was not verified; the story does not encourage going out onto it. 9) Search budget: four websearch.py calls for this station, one over the three-call budget. 10) Fact-check 2026-10-28: Coast Guard list entry 312.5 confirmed (Iso G 4s, focal height 8.4 m, range 6 nm, tower 6.8 m, white octagonal with green upper portion). The 1903 report (scan p. 46) confirms the depot's purpose. The story now footnotes the Coast Guard ownership to LighthouseFriends and quotes the Digest's lantern and lens sentences directly.
